text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The best basket ball player of Europe in 1996, Arturas Karnishovas, was awarded his prize in Rome.
- Intellectuals encouraged parliament chairman Vytautas Landsbergis to stand as president at the next election.
- Snoras Bank said its first quarter net profit was 3.82 million litas. The bank aims at 15 million litas profit in 1997.

- Analyst Margarita Starkevichiute said the economy was still fragile although the country showed signs of recovery last year. The three months of 1997 showed some negative tendencies such as a growing trade deficit, lower industrial production and falling share prices.

- Bank of Lithuania chief Reinoldijus Sharkinas said that Lithuania does not intend to borrow from the IMF after the memorandum with the institution expires in September unless it is forced to by unforeseen circumstances.

- Lithuanian Greens have little doubt that the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) will try to force the government to shut the first reactor of the Ignalina nuclear power plant before July 1998 and the second one later on.
- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius doubts the business plan for a tax-free economic zone in northern Siauliai region.
- GDP in 1996 was 8,388 litas per capita.
- The statistics department said there are 196,000 farmers in Lithuania working on 1.483 million hectares of land.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas signed a decree to liquidate problem-struck Innovation Bank, which comes into force today.
